avoid: Extended entries (price well above EMA-20 at entry) -- CONFIRMED LOSER historically (META Jul 15 at ~8.5% above EMA-20, stopped -8.04% Jul 23). LIVE TEST this week keeps LEANING AGAINST the thesis on a rebound tape: MSFT (entered Aug 3 at +15.5% above EMA20) firmed again to +3.27% (cushion 9.0%) and CRM (Aug 4, +7.2% ext) recovered to +3.48% (cushion 12.0%) -- both extended admits are now solidly green. Net: on this week's chop-then-rebound, extension has NOT been a clean loser -- 3 of 4 extended admits are green. Firm rule still stands as a sizing guard: treat >~6-8% above-EMA extension as size-DOWN or wait-for-pullback; when it co-occurs with a shallow cross (PDBC), SKIP outright. AMZN remains the weakest of the extended admits and a fast-death-cross watch, but no longer the acute one -- see XLE.

STACKED-FLAG entries (shallow cross + extended above EMA + thin liquidity together) -- RESOLVED as a SKIP, not a size-down: PDBC (0.15% cross + ~6.05% extended + thin liq, quarter-unit Jul 24) stopped out -2.40% Day 3. Distinguish from a SINGLE shallow-cross flag (BMY/GIS/CAG), a valid size-DOWN. Rule: one flag -> size down; two or more stacked -> skip. CRM (Aug 4) carried TWO soft flags (0.34% cross + 7.2% extended) but no thin-liq strike; taken via notional cap -- gave back its Day-1 green then RECOVERED to +3.48% by Day 3, so the two-soft-flag boundary test is now back to NEUTRAL-to-mildly-positive. Keep the one-flag-size-down / two-flag-skip rule as is.

NOTE: a cross below the floor at one snapshot can MATURE -- QQQ's cross widened 0.013%->0.224% intraday and was taken; NVDA's 0.07% flag matured to 0.350% by the Aug 5 scan. Re-check on the next scan rather than permanently blacklisting.

LEGACY intraday RSI buckets (informational, strategy retired): RSI 60-65 0/3, RSI 65-75 0/1, gap-up opens with RSI>60 -- all losers historically. Retained only as a record of why the intraday RSI approach was abandoned for trend-following.
